Quinolone classification: 3

A clinician discusses a respiratory fluoroquinolone with better pneumococcal activity than ciprofloxacin. Patient-specific safety and local susceptibility remain important before selection. Which listed agent is a standard example of this respiratory fluoroquinolone category?

  1. Moxifloxacin
  2. Agent-specific spectrum matters more than a generation label
  3. Levofloxacin
  4. Nalidixic acid
  5. Ciprofloxacin
Answer and explanation

Levofloxacin

Levofloxacin is a respiratory fluoroquinolone with improved pneumococcal activity; susceptibility and safety still govern selection.

Option explanations

Levofloxacin: Levofloxacin is a respiratory fluoroquinolone with improved pneumococcal activity; susceptibility and safety still govern selection.

Nalidixic acid: Nalidixic acid is an older first-generation quinolone with mainly urinary Gram-negative activity. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Ciprofloxacin: Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone with useful activity against susceptible Pseudomonas but weaker pneumococcal activity than respiratory fluoroquinolones. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Moxifloxacin: Moxifloxacin has respiratory and anaerobic activity but is not a preferred urinary agent and is not reliably antipseudomonal. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Agent-specific spectrum matters more than a generation label: Quinolone generation schemes vary; drug-specific coverage and safety determine clinical use. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
